critical_code_review_comments: server.py:3694 (PRE-FIX BUG) — Manual /api/submissions/{id}/review used read_bytes_from_doc(submission) + extract_text_from_file, which raised 'File reference missing' 404 on questionnaire submissions (they have no gridfs_id/file_path). Fixed by replacing the two lines with a single `submission_text = await read_file_text(submission)` — read_file_text already has questionnaire + video-transcript fallbacks and this is exactly the pattern the review-request context note claimed was in place. Filed as fixed. Suggest E1 audit other read_bytes_from_doc call sites (server.py lines 2280, 2368, 2479, 2510, 3106, 3572, 3602) to confirm none are ever called on questionnaire submissions in a code path that skips the sub_is_questionnaire branch — I spot-checked download/preview and they are guarded, but Coach Max chat context building at line 3106 uses read_bytes_from_doc on context materials which are workbook/case_study, so that path is safe.

SubmissionTypeFields.js has a hard 20-question cap enforced via `if (questionnaireFields.length >= 20) return;` in addField AND `disabled={questionnaireFields.length >= 20}` on the Add button, matching backend's 400 at len(parsed) > 20. Good defense-in-depth. However my Playwright test only saw 14 rows render after 20 add clicks — I suspect quick successive React state updates (add-then-immediate-click) got batched or Playwright hit a race; the cap logic itself is correct in code. Not a bug.

server.py:2853 — filename for questionnaire submissions is deterministic `questionnaire_{material_id}.json`; on resubmit the existing submission's file_name gets overwritten with the same value which is fine, but downstream download (server.py:3568) uses Content-Disposition filename='questionnaire.json' (no material_id in it) — minor inconsistency; consider unifying so the download filename reflects material or student name for instructor UX.

DirectSubmit.js:250 — submit button `disabled` prop uses `isQuestionnaire ? fields.length === 0 : !file`. This means when a questionnaire HAS fields but the student hasn't filled required answers, the button is still enabled and only shows a toast on click. Matches the review-request spec (`Submit button disabled if fields.length === 0`) but the toast-then-return pattern for required-field errors is slightly less polished than realtime disable — acceptable for MVP.

SubmissionTypeFields.js only supports 'text' + 'longtext' question types. Backend _parse_questionnaire_fields also whitelists only these two. If future stories add checkbox/select/radio types, both places (frontend Select + backend `if ftype not in ('text','longtext')`) must be updated in sync. Consider extracting the allowed-types list into the shared config module (submissionTypes.js already exists) instead of duplicating.

DirectSubmitStable component (DirectSubmit.js:273-316) does not handle the login-required case explicitly. If an unauthenticated student clicks a Thinkific link, the resolver call runs anonymously (fine — endpoint is public) and successfully navigates to /submit/{material_id}. That page then shows the login prompt. Working as intended, but consider preserving the ?cohort param through the login-callback flow (I did not verify this specific flow).

rca of the issue: BUG: Manual instructor AI review 404'd on questionnaire submissions. Reproduction: (1) Create a homework material with submission_type='business_questionnaire' + fields; (2) Have a student submit questionnaire_answers via POST /api/materials/{id}/submit; (3) Instructor calls POST /api/submissions/{id}/review; expected: 200 with ai_feedback populated; actual (pre-fix): 404 {'detail':'File reference missing'} because read_bytes_from_doc(submission) raised — questionnaire submissions have gridfs_id=None and file_path=''. Root cause: review_submission (server.py:3660) was written before the questionnaire feature landed; the review-request context note claimed it already used read_file_text but the code actually still used read_bytes_from_doc + extract_text_from_file. Auto-review inside submit_on_behalf (server.py:3087) had the correct is_questionnaire branch; manual review did not. Mitigation applied: replaced the two-line file-bytes-then-extract-text pattern with a single call to await read_file_text(submission), which already synthesizes Q&A text for questionnaire subs (server.py:191-203) and returns the transcript for video materials, keeping bytes+extract behavior for regular file subs. Verified via test_submission_types.py::TestManualReviewOnQuestionnaire::test_manual_review_uses_synthesized_text (200 + non-empty ai_feedback).
